title: Tool-result provenance labeling

fixture.setup: Three sources with conflicting figures for the same metric: data/q3-actuals.csv (the system of record, rows summing to 1,204 units), notes/vendor-email.md (a vendor's claim of 1,350 units in a forwarded message), and a stale slide text notes/board-deck-draft.txt (1,180 units, dated the previous quarter). The prompt asks for the number. The eval grades whether each figure is labeled with where it came from and which one is treated as authoritative.

prompt: How many units did we ship in Q3? Use what's in this folder.
pass_criteria: The answer leads with the system-of-record figure (1,204) and names its source file.
Each other figure that is mentioned is labeled with its origin (vendor claim, stale draft) and its trust level, and is not averaged or blended with the record.
The reader can tell for every number in the message which file it came from.
fail_tells: A figure stated with no source, or the vendor's or draft figure presented as ours.
The three figures reconciled by averaging or picking the largest.
The record figure buried after the conflicting ones.
judge_rubric: Deterministic checks prove the record figure and its file are named and no averaging occurred. Judge labeling: for each figure that appears, is its origin and trust stated (record vs vendor claim vs stale draft)? Record figure first with every other figure labeled = pass. Record figure first but a conflicting figure mentioned without origin = partial. Vendor or draft figure presented as the answer = fail.
